div.opener:
3, St. John's House,
THORNEY HOUSE
SMITH SQUARE
WESTMINSTER
LONDON.S.W.J.
June 17th. 1942. Dear Dr. Tillich,
div.p: I have just read with great interest your articles which appeared in the Protestant, and in the main I find myself in general agreement with the views you have so clearly expressed. I am not quite sure, however, whether you are in favour of a union of the English-speaking peoples as well as the federation of Europe, or whether you want Great Britain to be one of the members of the European federation.

I can't help feeling that in order to bring the United States permanently into a close association with Europe, the best approach would be through a World federation, of which the English-speaking peoples, the Soviet Union, a Far-Eastern federation, and a United States of Europe would be constituent members.

I am taking the liberty of sending you (under separate cover) a book which has recently been published in which I have endeavoured to
outline this proposal. I imagine that our views are more or less in common, and I shall be extremely grateful if you would send me your comments and criticisms after you have read the book.
I must apologise for inflicting myself upon you without any formal introduction.
div.closer:
Believe me to be,
Yours very sincerely, Davies. Dr.P. Tillich,
Union Theological Seminary,
3041,
Broadway,
New York.

postscript.p: P.S. I am also enclosing some particulars of the New Commonwealth Society which you may find of interest. D.
